title: Science Feast 2025 : Come defy our cardboard AI !
background_paragraph: I participated to the 2025 edition of the Fête de la Science at the University of Strasbourg. I animated a stand destined to teach the concepts of artificial intelligence using no computed of any device of any sort. Our stand was called Viens défier nos IA en carton ! (come defy our cardboard AI).
background_ttt_paragraph: The first workshop is based on the tic-tac-toe game. It allows us to illustrate the concept of decision taking by an AI. In order to do so, we play a round against a voluntary participant. We always take the role of the AI while the participant plays the role of a human. On each turn, we always play according the a specific decision tree (shown on the top-left on Figure 2). The human player is not complused to use the decision tree. This workshop allows us to explain how an AI thinks (or in reality how it does not think !).
background_nim_paragraph: The second workshop is based on a variation of the game of Nim. It allows us to illustrate the learning process of an AI using cups and tokens. We play a few rounds agains a willing participant. Firstly, we explain the rules and let the human player play against a trainer AI (unbeatable in this scenario). After a few rounds, we invite the public to play against an untrained AI. We show from round to round how the AI learns from its mistakes depending on the choices made by the human player. Finally, we show a naked version of the AI which reveals its choices (aka its decision tree) and we explain how the previously played rounds make the decision tree converge toward this single solution.
background_links_paragraph: I have developed a numerical version of those workshops in order to keep a trace. If you want to try a game of tic-tac-toe against an AI using the appropriate decision tree, you can visit this page. If you want to try yourself on the game of Nim and visualize the learning process in real-time, you can visit this page.
